answer: Agents could stake a scarce, nontransferable work credential earned by completing randomly assigned tasks, then post a bond before entering a market. A sonnet, falcon, or sable-themed task is still checked against hidden test cases; passing raises the credential’s rate limit, while failed or duplicated submissions forfeit part of the bond. Creating many identities therefore does not multiply trusted capacity: each one needs costly work and locked capital, and detection burns the attacker’s stake.
